standard_prerequisites.name: Fundamental sequences and countable limit ordinals
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every countable limit ordinal lambda has a strictly increasing cofinal sequence (delta_n) of ordinals below lambda.

standard_prerequisites.name: Scattered orders, Hausdorff rank and Z^alpha
standard_prerequisites.statement: Standard Hausdorff analysis of scattered linear orders and the cited bound that a scattered order of Hausdorff rank below lambda has Scott sentence complexity below Pi^in_lambda (Alvir-Rossegger, cited at source line 1416); the back-and-forth behaviour of Z^alpha-multiples is the article's own lemma, delivered here with its complete proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Parameter-definable interval lower bound
standard_prerequisites.statement: The cited criterion that a Delta^in_0-definable interval over parameters cannot exceed the Scott rank of the ambient structure (Montalban, cited at source line 1421); used only for the optimality step.

core_obligations: Build L_lambda as the sum over i in omega of i + Z^{delta_n} from a fundamental sequence of lambda, and verify the three defining features of the order: exactly one 1-block isomorphic to each natural number, those blocks ordered like omega, and the interval between successive blocks isomorphic to Z^{delta_n} (source lines 1403-1411).

Express the three features by an infinitary sentence of complexity below lambda: the first two by finitely many quantifier alternations, and the third by relativising the Scott sentence of Z^{delta_n} to the described interval, which is below lambda because the Hausdorff rank of the interval is (source lines 1412-1417).

Prove optimality: the Z^{delta_n} have unbounded Scott rank below lambda by the delivered Z-power lemma, they are Delta^in_0-definable over parameters in L_lambda, so the cited parameter-definable-interval bound gives SR(L_lambda) at least delta_n for every n and hence Scott sentence complexity exactly Pi^in_lambda (source lines 1419-1421).

proof_roadmap.step: Statement and complete proof of the article's own Z-power back-and-forth lemma, delivered as local support.
The immediately following author proof of prop:scatteredlimit.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the existence of a scattered linear order of Scott sentence complexity Pi^in_lambda for every limit ordinal lambda (statement, source lines 1397-1399), witnessed by the explicit order L_lambda = sum_{i in omega} i + Z^{delta_n} built from a fundamental sequence (source line 1403). The non-routine parts are the three-clause Pi^in_lambda description, in particular the relativisation of the Scott sentence of Z^{delta_n} to the interval it bounds (1414-1416), and the optimality step, which needs both the article's Z-power lemma for the unbounded ranks below lambda and the cited parameter-definable-interval bound (1419-1421). The order is not a shuffle sum, so the article's shuffle-sum lower-bound corollary cannot be used here, and the interval description has to be read off the construction itself.
